commonPreconditions.A: Account A (sender) exists, 2FA disabled, English UI, credentials in .env
commonPreconditions.B: Account B (receiver) exists, 2FA disabled, English UI, credentials in .env
commonPreconditions.OUT: User is signed out (empty browser storage)
commonPreconditions.PUB: No account needed; public page https://proton.me/mail reachable

testCases.scenario: Hero presents the privacy value proposition, trust signals and both acquisition paths
testCases.expected: Page served (< 400); title contains "Proton Mail"; H1 "Secure email that protects your privacy"; value proposition (encrypted, Switzerland); trust signals (100 million users, app rating, recommended by experts); "Create a free account" and "Get Mail for Business" visible
testCases.reason: First impression and conversion point for every visitor; a broken hero blocks all acquisition

testCases.scenario: "Create a free account" starts the free sign-up flow
steps: Click "Create a free account" (nothing is entered)
testCases.expected: Proton account sign-up page opens
testCases.reason: Main acquisition funnel; checked without creating accounts

testCases.scenario: Returning user reaches the sign-in form from the page header
testCases.expected: account.proton.me sign-in with username, password and enabled "Sign in" button
testCases.reason: Only public path into the mailbox; links the public page to the AUTH-* tests

testCases.scenario: Plans offer Proton Unlimited, a recommended Mail Plus and a free plan without credit card
steps: Scroll to "Proton Mail plans for your privacy"
testCases.expected: Cards for Proton Unlimited, Mail Plus, Proton Free, each with its CTA; Free shows 0.00 and "No credit card required"; Mail Plus marked Recommended
testCases.reason: Revenue-relevant content; asserts structure and rules, not exact prices (region/promotion dependent)

testCases.scenario: Switching billing period re-prices Mail Plus and restores the yearly price
steps: Select "12 months", read Mail Plus price
testCases.expected: 12 months shows "every 12 months" billing note; 1 month shows a different price without it; switching back restores the yearly price
testCases.reason: State transition on pricing, both directions; wrong prices are a business and legal risk

testCases.scenario: Choosing Mail Plus leads to sign-up / checkout for that plan
testCases.expected: Proton account sign-up / checkout opens for the paid plan
testCases.reason: Paid conversion funnel entry point

testCases.scenario: Changing currency re-prices the plans
steps: Change currency from USD to EUR
testCases.expected: Selector shows EUR; plan prices shown in euro
testCases.reason: International customers; currency state must propagate to all prices

testCases.scenario: "Get Mail for Business" leads to the business offering
testCases.expected: Business page opens
testCases.reason: B2B acquisition funnel

testCases.scenario: FAQ lists all six questions; answers expand and collapse
testCases.expected: Six questions listed; the answer expands, then collapses
testCases.reason: Self-service information that reduces support load; interaction state is verifiable

testCases.scenario: Footer exposes legal links, company identity, language selector and current copyright
testCases.expected: Privacy Policy and Terms & conditions link to legal pages; Proton AG, Geneva, Switzerland; language selector; "© <current year> Proton AG"
testCases.reason: Legal/compliance obligations; stale copyright or broken legal links are visible quality issues

testCases.scenario: Phone layout: menu reveals Sign in, hero usable, no horizontal scrolling
steps: Open https://proton.me/mail on a phone profile
testCases.expected: H1 in viewport, "Create a free account" visible, page fits the width; menu shows "Sign in"
testCases.reason: Large share of visitors are mobile; layout-level checks are stable

testCases.scenario: Feature carousel, imagery and visual design
steps: Review sections and carousel on desktop and phone
testCases.expected: Content readable, carousel navigates, images load
testCases.reason: Marketing visuals change often; pixel/visual assertions would be brittle and low value

testCases.scenario: Page health: no console errors or failed first-party requests
testCases.expected: No console errors; no proton.me request >= 400
testCases.reason: Backlog: needs an allow-list for third-party noise before it is reliable

testCases.scenario: Page in other languages via the language selector
testCases.expected: Page content and links localised
testCases.reason: Translation quality needs human review

testCases.scenario: Valid credentials open the mailbox; session survives a page reload
steps: Enter valid username and password, tick 'Keep me signed in'
testCases.expected: Inbox (/u/<n>/inbox) is shown with the Compose button; after reload the user is still signed in and not redirected to sign-in
testCases.reason: Gatekeeper for every other journey; stable and cheap

testCases.scenario: Invalid credentials are rejected
steps: Enter unknown username and wrong password
testCases.expected: 'Incorrect login credentials' error; user stays on the sign-in form; no mailbox URL reached
testCases.reason: Security-relevant negative path; deterministic; needs no account

testCases.scenario: Empty sign-in form shows required-field validation
testCases.expected: 'This field is required' shown, username field focused, no navigation
testCases.reason: Boundary/validation case; fast; no account needed

testCases.scenario: Sign-out ends the session; Back does not reopen the mailbox
testCases.expected: Sign-in page after sign-out, after Back, and after direct navigation; cached mail is never displayed
testCases.reason: Session-termination security behaviour; state transition

testCases.scenario: Sign-in with 2FA (TOTP) enabled
testCases.expected: Mailbox opens only after a valid code; invalid code rejected
testCases.reason: Needs a TOTP secret in the test environment; storing it in automation weakens the account's security. Candidate for automation only with a dedicated secrets vault

testCases.scenario: Repeated failed sign-ins trigger human verification / rate limiting
testCases.expected: Proton throttles and presents human verification
testCases.reason: Automating it would hammer a production service and must never attempt to bypass CAPTCHA

testCases.scenario: Session revoked from another device signs this browser out
testCases.preconditions: A signed in on two browsers
steps: Revoke session from Settings > Security on browser 2
testCases.expected: Browser 1 is signed out at next server call
testCases.reason: Would invalidate cached sessions used by the rest of the suite; low regression frequency

testCases.scenario: Two-account send: B receives with correct sender, subject and body
testCases.testData: Unique subject 'Automation Assessment [PMA-<run>] COMP-001 <rnd>' and body
steps: A: Compose to B, enter subject and body
A: Verify 'Message sent' and message in Sent
B: Wait for delivery to Inbox
testCases.expected: B sees A's address as sender, the exact subject and body
testCases.reason: Core business journey end-to-end across two mailboxes

testCases.scenario: Send blocked for a malformed recipient address
steps: Compose with malformed recipient, subject, body
testCases.expected: Invalid-address validation shown; composer stays open; no 'Message sent'
testCases.reason: Negative validation; protects against silent mis-sends

testCases.scenario: Send blocked when no recipient is given
steps: Compose with subject and body only
testCases.expected: Missing-recipient validation shown; composer stays open; nothing sent
testCases.reason: Boundary (empty) case of the same rule, different validation branch

testCases.scenario: CC visible to recipients, BCC hidden
testCases.testData: To: B, CC: A, BCC: A+bcc alias
steps: A: Compose with To, CC and BCC
B: Open the delivered message header
testCases.expected: B sees A in CC; the BCC alias does not appear anywhere in B's header
testCases.reason: Privacy-critical: a BCC leak is a high-impact defect

testCases.scenario: Password-protected email to an external recipient
steps: Open link in external mailbox and decrypt
testCases.expected: Recipient needs the password; message decrypts correctly
testCases.reason: Needs a non-Proton mailbox and link handling outside the app; better as a periodic exploratory check

testCases.scenario: Subject/body boundaries: empty subject warning, very long subject, unicode/emoji
testCases.expected: Empty subject prompts confirmation; long/unicode subjects preserved
testCases.reason: Backlog: data-driven extension of COMP-001 (lower risk, deferred to keep suite at 20)

testCases.scenario: Rich-text formatting renders consistently for the recipient
testCases.expected: Formatting preserved
testCases.reason: Visual fidelity check; brittle in UI automation, better covered by component tests or manual review

testCases.scenario: Auto-save to Drafts without closing composer; persists after full reload
steps: Open composer, type subject and body (do not close)
testCases.expected: Draft listed while composer is still open; after reload it reopens with the same subject and body
testCases.reason: Data-loss risk; tests true server-side auto-save, not just save-on-close

testCases.scenario: Reopen, edit, reload, then send: draft moves from Drafts to Sent
testCases.expected: Edit persists across reload; after sending the draft is gone from Drafts and present in Sent
testCases.reason: Full draft state transition (draft -> edited -> sent)

testCases.scenario: Delete draft removes it permanently
testCases.expected: Draft not listed before or after reload
testCases.reason: Destructive action must be final and server-side

testCases.scenario: Draft with attachment keeps the attachment after reload
testCases.expected: Attachment still listed with the same name
testCases.reason: Backlog: combines DRAFT-001 and ATT-001 building blocks; deferred to stay within 15-20 tests

testCases.scenario: Same draft edited concurrently in two tabs
steps: Open same draft in two tabs
testCases.expected: Conflict handled without silent data loss
testCases.reason: Behaviour is not clearly specified; exploratory investigation gives more value

testCases.scenario: Unread -> read on open -> mark unread
testCases.expected: Row unread, then read after opening, then unread again
testCases.reason: Most frequent user action; read state drives counters and notifications

testCases.scenario: Star / unstar updates Starred folder
testCases.expected: Message listed in Starred after starring and absent after unstarring
testCases.reason: Verifies derived-folder state, not just icon toggle

testCases.scenario: Inbox -> Archive -> Trash -> restore to Inbox
steps: B: from Archive move to Trash
B: from Trash move to Inbox
testCases.expected: After every move the message is in exactly the target folder and absent from the source
testCases.reason: State-transition coverage of all core move actions incl. restore

testCases.scenario: Bulk select and move several messages
testCases.expected: All 3 moved, none left behind
testCases.reason: Backlog: needs 3 deliveries per run (slow); single-message moves already cover the action logic

testCases.scenario: Create custom folder, move message into it, delete folder
testCases.expected: Message listed in folder; folder removal handled
testCases.reason: Backlog: free plan folder limits make cleanup mandatory; next candidate after current 20

testCases.scenario: Apply and remove a label
testCases.expected: Message listed under label only while applied
testCases.reason: Backlog, same reasoning as FOLDER-001

testCases.scenario: Keyword search returns exactly the match; clear restores folder view
testCases.expected: Exactly one result with the subject; URL holds keyword; after clear the keyword is gone and Inbox lists the message
testCases.reason: Primary retrieval path; exact-result assertion catches over- and under-matching

testCases.scenario: Advanced search: keyword AND sender (plus no-result case)
testCases.testData: Same token in two messages from A and from B
steps: Seed message A->B and B->B with same token
testCases.expected: Only A's message returned; unknown sender gives 'No results'
testCases.reason: Multi-condition search with discriminating data proves the AND logic; includes no-result behaviour

testCases.scenario: Date-range search
testCases.expected: Only messages inside range
testCases.reason: Needs aged data that cannot be created on demand through the UI

testCases.scenario: Body content search with client-side index enabled
testCases.expected: Message found by body text
testCases.reason: Requires building a local encrypted index (slow, device-specific)

testCases.scenario: Subject filter moves matching mail to Archive; non-matching stays in Inbox
testCases.preconditions: A; B; no other suite filter
steps: B: create filter (subject contains token -> Archive)
A: send matching and non-matching mail
testCases.expected: Matching message only in Archive; non-matching in Inbox; filter removed afterwards
testCases.reason: Rule behaviour validated with both matching and non-matching data

testCases.scenario: Disabled filter no longer applies; edit changes behaviour
testCases.expected: Disabled filter has no effect
testCases.reason: Backlog: adds two more deliveries; free plan allows a single filter so runs must be serial

testCases.scenario: Sieve (advanced) filter syntax
testCases.expected: Valid scripts saved, invalid rejected
testCases.reason: Paid feature; syntax validation is cheaper to test below the UI

testCases.scenario: Upload, send and receive an attachment with the same file name
steps: A: compose to B, attach file
testCases.expected: Composer lists the file; message in Sent; B sees attachment 'attachment.txt'
testCases.reason: Attachments are encrypted client-side - high-risk path

testCases.scenario: Remove attachment before sending
testCases.expected: Received message has no attachment
testCases.reason: Backlog

testCases.scenario: Attachment over the size limit is rejected
testCases.expected: Clear size-limit error; nothing uploaded
testCases.reason: Uploading large encrypted files is slow and bandwidth-heavy for every run

testCases.scenario: Download received attachment and verify content
testCases.expected: Downloaded file identical to original
testCases.reason: Backlog: preview/download UX varies by file type; to be added once the download control is confirmed

testCases.scenario: Undo Send: transient undo state, restored composer, final send after window
steps: Verify composer content and Sent folder
Send again and let the undo window expire
testCases.expected: Undo restores the composer and nothing is in Sent; after the window closes the message is in Sent
testCases.reason: Timing-dependent flow synchronised on observable states, not sleeps

testCases.scenario: Schedule send for tomorrow, verify Scheduled state, cancel via Edit
testCases.expected: Message in Scheduled with banner; after Edit it is a draft and no longer scheduled
testCases.reason: Covers scheduled state without waiting for real time to pass

testCases.scenario: Scheduled message is actually delivered at the scheduled time
testCases.expected: Delivered at (not before) scheduled time
testCases.reason: Long-running wall-clock test; belongs in a nightly job using API-level scheduling with a short custom time or a controllable clock

testCases.scenario: Visual layout, themes and responsive breakpoints
steps: Review UI at several viewports and themes
testCases.expected: No visual breakage
testCases.reason: Pixel comparisons against a frequently changing production UI produce noise, not signal

testCases.scenario: Keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels
steps: Navigate mailbox and composer by keyboard / screen reader
testCases.expected: All actions reachable and announced
testCases.reason: Human judgement needed; could later add automated axe scans as a separate layer
